assumptions: n <= 10^6 for T-C09-A; factorisations for n <= 2e5 for T-C09-B

floating-point evaluation of nu'(n) = n psi + n*: safe because the only exact boundary hits are n = 1 (nu' = psi^2) and n = 2 (nu' = psi^3), both irreducible, and otherwise |nu'(n) - boundary| = |(n-1) psi - p| >= 0.4/n >> 1e-10 for n <= 1e6 (psi badly approximable)
meta.falsification: A reducible n with f outside (0.2361, 0.8541); a factorisation longer than the bound.
meta.hypothesis: T-C09-A: if f = frac((n+1)/phi) lies outside (psi^2... precisely outside (1/phi - psi^2, 1/phi - psi^3) = (0.2361, 0.8541), then n is circle-irreducible; such n have density 1/phi^2. T-C09-B: every factorisation of n into r irreducibles satisfies |nu'(n)| < |psi|^r, where nu'(n) = n*psi + n*.
meta.methodology: Scan n <= 10^6: compute f exactly via integer square roots; check every n with f outside the product zone is irreducible; measure densities by scale; within the product zone measure the irreducible fraction. For T-C09-B compare max factorisation length with log|nu'|/log|psi|.
